bib.title: Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory", Boqin Yuan (UC San Diego), Yue Su (Carnegie Mellon), Kun Yao (UNC). ICLR 2026 conference paper (page header); arXiv 2603.02473v2, cs.AI, 12 Apr 2026.

COVERAGE: 10 of 10 pages, 26,302 of 26,302 chars, including appendices A-D. Extraction was clean. Figure captions were not run; figure content was read from the captions in the text only. No embedded instructions found.

MAIN CLAIM: In prompt-based agent memory on LoCoMo, the retrieval method matters far more than the write strategy. Raw chunks (zero LLM calls) match or beat Mem0-style fact extraction and MemGPT-style summarization. Most failures occur at retrieval, not at utilization.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
Shared setup: LoCoMo, 10 conversations, 1,540 non-adversarial questions. Backbone GPT-5-mini, text-embedding-3-small, k=5. 3x3 grid of write strategy by retrieval method (cosine, BM25, hybrid+rerank with GPT-5.2 as reranker). LLM-judge accuracy. One run per cell is reported; no variance is given.
1. Average accuracy by retrieval method is 57.1% (BM25), 73.4% (cosine) and 77.2% (hybrid), a 20-point spread. Across write strategies the spread within a retrieval column is only 3-8 points (Table 1, p3).
2. Basic RAG (raw 3-turn chunks) scores 77.9% with cosine and 81.1% with hybrid. Extracted Facts scores 72.2% and 77.3%. Summarized Episodes scores 70.1% and 73.3%. The exception is BM25, where Summarized Episodes (62.7%) beats Basic RAG (59.2%).
3. Precision@5 against accuracy across the nine configs gives r=0.98 (n=9 points, Fig 3, p3-4).
4. Failure shares (% of all questions, Table 2). Retrieval failure runs 11.4-46.3% (Extracted Facts + BM25 is 46.3%). Hybrid cuts Basic RAG retrieval failure from 35.3% (BM25) to 11.4%. Utilization failure is 3.9-8.1% and hallucination 0.4-1.4%. The memory "beneficial" rate is 79.0% for Basic RAG + hybrid.
Judge validation (App. D): LLM judge vs. human on answer correctness, 200 samples, 92% agreement, kappa 0.82. Failure classification, 200 incorrect answers, 85% agreement, with most confusion between retrieval and utilization failure.

QUOTES
- "On LoCoMo, retrieval method is the dominant factor: average accuracy spans 20 points across retrieval methods (57.1% to 77.2%) but only 3–8 points across write strategies." (p1, abstract)
- "Raw chunked storage, which requires zero LLM calls, matches or outperforms expensive lossy alternatives" (p1, abstract)
- "Our study evaluates a single backbone model (GPT-5-mini) on one benchmark (LoCoMo) with a fixed retrieval budget (k=5), limiting generality." (p4)

LIMITS
- Single model, single benchmark, fixed k=5.
- Write strategies are prompt-based reimplementations, not the actual Mem0 or MemGPT systems. Learned (RL) memory such as MEM1 and Mem-alpha is out of scope.
- The raw-chunk advantage "may also diminish under tighter context budgets where compression is required" (p4).
- Correctness and failure labels come from LLM judges.
- Write-time information loss is not measured directly (App. B). "Retrieval failure" lumps together "not retrieved" and "never stored in enough detail", so the write-versus-retrieval split in failures is blurred.
- Utilization is judged only where a relevant memory was retrieved.
- The r=0.98 rests on 9 points and is a correlation, not causal.
- Token F1 barely tracks the 20-point accuracy gap (0.221 vs 0.168).
- No cost or latency figures beyond the LLM-call counts in Table 3.
- The paper says portions of the text were LLM-edited.

BUILDS ON
- MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023, arXiv:2310.08560).
- Mem0 (Chhikara et al., 2025, arXiv:2504.19413).
- A-MEM (Xu et al., 2025, arXiv:2502.12110).
- MemoryBank (Zhong et al., 2023).
- RAG (Lewis et al., NeurIPS 2020).
- LoCoMo (Maharana et al., ACL 2024).
- Benchmarks it cites: LongMemEval (Wu et al., 2025), MemoryAgentBench (Hu et al., 2025), RealTalk (Lee et al., 2025).
- RL memory: MEM1 (Zhou et al., 2025), Mem-alpha (Wang et al., 2025).

FIGURE CANDIDATE
- Fig 2 (p2): accuracy across the 3x3 grid at k=5. Columns (retrieval) differ by 14-23 points; rows (write strategy) by 3-8 points. It shows the main result at a glance.
- Alternative: Fig 4 (p4), retrieval failure rate by retrieval method.

NOTE FOR NOTE 06-memory.md: this supports "invest in retrieval before write-time sophistication" and counts as a sharpens-type citation. Always state the caveats: GPT-5-mini, LoCoMo, k=5, and one run per cell with no variance reported.
